newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening higher.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening slightly lower Monday, in line with the bullion market which was off its overnight highs in London midday.
But the U.S. dollar lost more ground against most major currencies early Monday and the slide is likely to underpin last week's gains precious metals markets, analysts said.

Part of the reason for the fall in gold prices in the past year to four year lows has been the steady rise in the U.S. dollar, making gold more expensive in many currencies, but this may now be being reversed, analysts said.
Robust physical offtake is also providing support, with Indian wedding season demand pushing gold higher in the Bombay bullion market, analyts noted.
European central were also unlikely to sell more gold this year, according to South African central bank governor, Chris Stals, Monday.

But, while gold looks like it may have seen its lows for the year, after finding support around $340 an ounce, in the past month for the second time this year, producing hedging is still seen slowing any rally.
COMEX June was seen opening unchanged to down 50 cents an ounce from Friday's close at $349.30.
Spot gold was quoted early around $347.20/70, compared to the London Monday morning fix at $348.20, the highest fix for a month, and the New York close Friday around $347.80/30.
COMEX gold stocks slipped 793 ounces to 910,084 ounces Friday, while silver stocks fell 480,894 ounces to 190,876,850 ounces.
COMEX July silver was seen opening unchanged to down 0.3 cent from the previous close at $4.880.

NYMEX July platinum was seen opening unchanged to down 50 cents from the previous close at $389.40 an ounce, while NYMEX June palladium was called to open unchanged to up 50 cents from Friday's close at 163.90.

In London Monday platinum and palladium caught up with Friday's NYMEX action and fixed at 395.25 an ounce in the case of platinum, the highest since February 28, while palladium was fixed at its highest level since April 20, 1995 at $171.75. ((Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, 212-959-1640))
